# `enabled` reference

<Warning>

This page documents a **draft** for a feature gated behind the `enabled_meta_argument` experiment, not yet released in any stable version of Terraform. Refer to the [`terraform` block's `experiments` argument](/terraform/language/block/terraform#experiments) and the [Terraform changelog](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the current status.

</Warning>

Use `enabled` to turn a resource or module's single instance on or off, without changing how it's addressed. The common alternative, `count = <condition> ? 1 : 0`, works but makes the address conditionally indexed (`aws_instance.example[0]`), which forces a `terraform state mv` whenever the condition flips and requires index-aware syntax everywhere the resource is referenced.

## Usage

`enabled` accepts any value, of any type, and never errors. `null`, `false`, an empty string, and an empty list/set/map/tuple/object all mean disabled. Any other value — including the number `0` — means enabled:

```hcl
variable "alarm_email" {
  default = null
}

resource "aws_sns_topic_subscription" "alarm" {
  enabled  = var.alarm_email
  endpoint = var.alarm_email
}
```

No comparison is needed: leaving `alarm_email` unset disables the subscription; setting it enables one.

You can't combine `enabled` with `count` or `for_each` on the same block.

## Referring to a disabled instance

A disabled resource or module evaluates to `null`, not an empty list or map, so it stays object-shaped whether it exists or not:

```hcl
output "topic_arn" {
  value = try(aws_sns_topic_subscription.alarm.id, null)
}
```

## Scope

`enabled` is well-suited to a resource that should exist only once some value has been supplied. It's not a fit for the opposite case — a module that creates a fallback resource only when the caller *didn't* supply one — since a bare value can't tell those two intentions apart. For that pattern, have the child module accept the possibly-null override directly and resolve the decision internally, so callers never express the condition at all.

`enabled` values must be known before Terraform performs remote operations, and can't be sensitive, for the same reasons that apply to `for_each`.

## Supported constructs

- [`resource` blocks](/terraform/language/block/resource)
- [`data` blocks](/terraform/language/block/data)
- [`ephemeral` blocks](/terraform/language/block/ephemeral)
- [`module` blocks](/terraform/language/block/module)

Not supported in `action` blocks.
